method: One serialized process per VSync mode/revision. Synthetic SDL input is polled by the actual application. All compilation and other graphics probes had finished. Seed 42, radius 1, generator 1, temporary survival world; no user world/settings/mods.
limitations: CPU scopes are inclusive; events, bindings, styles and layout can nest within runtime/DrawList scopes. Do not sum every scope. Initial load/rebuild also includes work not split into every internal phase.
Whole frame is poll plus application frame call. This is not input-to-photon latency or isolated GPU execution time.

GPU data is the previous submission's interval between BOTTOM_OF_PIPE timestamps around UI commands. Pipeline/queue overlap and clock state affect it; it is not isolated UI shader execution and does not measure CPU rasterization.

VSync flags are requested policies: FIFO for on, preference for IMMEDIATE then MAILBOX then FIFO for off. Effective selected mode was not separately logged. Acquisition, presentation and fence waits are distinct CPU scopes.

Hyprland tiled the requested window to 947x1019. Resize rows measure requests, not completed resize. Actual resize/minimize/restore were separately verified in an isolated KWin virtual Wayland compositor.
The click workload changes TextInput focus; pause/resume activates actual UI buttons with Enter. Pointer button activation correctness has CPU regression coverage, not a separate latency row.
Health updates use the real host adapter/renderer with deterministic snapshots, outside the simulation, and are explicitly labeled host_fixture.

One serialized run per revision/mode, 240 samples, unpinned GPU/CPU clocks on normal desktop. Idle median slightly regresses; no uniform improvement or statistical significance claim. Interrupted after/on run was discarded and rerun completely.

Native geometry uses a bounded 2048-square atlas. Warm hover/text/rapid typing upload zero atlas bytes. New glyphs/resources may upload an atlas page; this is not a full-screen UI raster. Compilation, query reads and recording remain CPU work.
